judged_text: add_members silently skips any username that does not match a user and still renders success_json, so a partially-applied batch is indistinguishable from a successful one. An admin who submits 'alice,bob' with a typo sees the member list reload without bob and no error anywhere; the only documentation of this behavior was the 'succeeds silently' tests this diff deletes.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record; unknown/typoed usernames are simply skipped, and the action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds. This makes partial application indistinguishable from full success, matching the finding. The diff also removes prior specs that explicitly asserted “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users,” so the behavior is now less documented/covered, but it’s not provably an outright defect from the diff alone (could be intentional).
